subject: humanities
passage: For thousands of years, Aboriginal peoples of Australia's Western Desert created designs in sand, on rock, and on their bodies, often for ceremonies. In 1971, at the settlement of Papunya, a group of senior men began painting such designs with acrylic paint on boards and, later, on canvas. <u>Because these works could be moved, sold, and exhibited, they carried Western Desert imagery far beyond the communities where it had been made.</u> Within two decades, paintings in this style hung in major museums, though some artists took care to alter or hide designs considered too sacred for outsiders to see.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains a consequence of the change in materials described just before it.
choices.B: It describes the ceremonies for which the earliest desert designs were originally made.
choices.C: It explains why some artists hid certain designs from outside viewers.
choices.D: It argues that the new paintings were less meaningful than the older designs.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one describes a change: designs once made in sand, on rock, and on bodies were now painted on boards and canvas. The underlined sentence begins "Because these works could be moved, sold, and exhibited," and tells what followed from that change: the imagery spread far beyond its home communities.
explanation.A: Correct. Portable paintings could travel, so the sentence explains how the new materials carried the imagery to distant audiences.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the older designs were often made for ceremonies but never describes those ceremonies.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Hiding sacred designs is mentioned only in the last sentence; the underlined sentence is about how the paintings spread, not about concealment.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never judges the new paintings as less meaningful; this claims far more than it says.
